# Anchorlaw — Code Verification on DeepSeek Harness
**English | 中文**

> **"Any claim must have a verifiable practice anchor."**
>
> — First Law, Materialist Practice Theo

**"Any claim must have a verifiable practice anchor."**
>
> — First Law, Materialist Practice Theory
Anchorlaw is a **code verification toolchain for AI-assisted (vibe) coding**, maintained as a **Deep
Seek Harness (DSH) host adaptation**: the `dsh/` subtree ships 11 protocol skills, 4 model tools, an
d the `anchorlaw` agent preset — install once, and every DSH session gets scan / report / noise-card
/ AI-context tooling. The underlying protocol (`spec/`, `python/`, `typescript/`) is language-neutr
al and drives the DSH tools. The Reasonix host format is **archived, not maintained** — see Reasonix
DSH tools. The Reasonix host format is **archived, not maintained** — see Reasonix Version Archive.
## Quick Start (DSH)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Project-scoped skills need no installer: place them under `<projectRoot>/.dsh/skills/` (DSH's native
project root, rank 100) and any preset discovers them. DSH has no project-level plugin/preset mecha
nism, so the `anchorlaw` preset and the 4 tools are host-level only.
> Tools appear in **new** sessions (session composition is fixed at creation). The global mount is g
ated by a tool-schema check (2026-08-13 incident guard) — a malformed schema can never be installed.
## What You Get (DSH)
### 4 model tools — global, every session
| Tool | What it does |
| `anchorlaw_scan` | Level-1 defensive-pattern scanner (P1-P6; `lang` cpp/go/java → annotation extra

ction) |
| `anchorlaw_report` | Health report (scan findings + noise backlog + verdict) |
| `anchorl

aw_ai_context` | Noise cards + curriculum export for LLM context injection |
| `anchorlaw_status` |
Toolchain versions + discovered `anchor-*` skills |
### 11 protocol skills (`anchor-*`, DSH format)
L0-L4 action skills + execution roles (scout/worker/judge), loaded per scenario; skill bodies live i
n `dsh/skills/` (single source of truth, protocol §14 is the host-neutral spec). Trigger index and t
ool-call conventions: `dsh/AGENTS.md`.
### anchorlaw agent preset
Judge-driven four-stage pipeline persona (protocol §15.4): input contract → implementation spec → pl
an → parallel implementation → delivery. Acceptance criteria first, 3-round hard stop, `confirmed` g
ranted **only by the human**; scout/worker/judge delegated through isolated subagents.
## Protocol Core (language-neutral backend)
The protocol itself lives at the repo root and is host-neutral — the DSH tools drive its CLI:

*Python** | `python/anchorlaw-scanner` + `python/anchorlaw` | Scanner (verified) + anchors/noise/CLI

(experimental) — the DSH tool backend |

canner (in development) |

mat defined, no A/B test |

> **Honesty notice**: Components marked EXPERIMENTAL, UNVERIFIED, or CONJECTURE are working hypothes
es. Their value has not been demonstrated through practice. Use them to help us test the hypotheses
— not because we claim they work.
### Changelog
> **v0.25 (2026-10-24):** DSH host-adaptation follow-ups for 0.2.1 — ① Upstream removed the `./list-
agents` subpath export from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control` (it registered the shared contr
ol tools together in the package's main entry), so the preset's `tool-subagent-list-agents` row reso
lved to nothing (`ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`). The row is gone; the `list_agents` tool stays ava
ilable through the `tool-subagent-control` row, matching upstream's own preset. The fail-closed row
gate caught this at maintenance time rather than at session mount — exactly why it exists. ② The DSH
bundle now declares `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.0`): the runtime prefers an own `engines.dsh` over `peerDe
pendencies`, so an incompatible harness fails closed instead of loading the bundle against silently
wrong host APIs — the failure mode behind both the 0.1.7 and the 0.2.x incidents. (`^0.2.1` was reje
cted as a range: a `0.2.1-rc.N` prerelease sorts before its release and would not match.) The protoc

ol core is unchanged — this is §16 host-adaptation scope.
>
> **v0.24 (2026-10-17):** DSH host-adapt
ation follow-ups for 0.2.x — two pieces of stale host configuration, both of which the existing gate
s reported as green. ① Upstream DSH 0.2.x deleted the `cwd` prompt variable, while persona templates
interpolate **strictly at assembly**, so the `anchorlaw` preset failed on every request with `unkno
wn prompt variable "{{cwd}}" in section "deployment:persona-prefix"`; the working directory now arri
ves as the `working-directory:current` runtime context, and a new fail-closed gate (`dsh/tests/audit
_prompt_variables.mjs`, self-check item 7) requires every `{{variable}}` in a preset template to be
registered by the running harness — the preset-row gate could not see this class, because rows resol
ved and packages mounted while the template variable was already dead. ② The `backgroundMode` key on
the subagent rows no longer exists in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent`; Schemastery ignores unknown
keys, so it was silently dropped and never had any effect — removed. The protocol core is unchanged

— this is §16 host-adaptation scope.
